subject: Candidate cadence & bar standards: Liam Porter — Senior Serving Engineer
messages:
From: Sarah McKenna <sarah@talentbridge.io>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 15:07:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Liam Porter — Senior Serving Engineer candidate

Hi Connor,

Quick intro — Liam Porter is a candidate I'm presenting for the Senior Serving Engineer role you posted. He has experience shipping inference runtimes at scale (former infra lead at RivenAI), plus kernel-level performance work on quantized transformer inference. Resume attached.

A few notes from my screen:
- Availability: candidate is flexible next week (PST mornings ideal)
- Current comp expectations: in band for senior/early staff (glassdoor-based)
- Interested in production-facing roles and cross-team ownership

If you're interested I can lock a panel; would you prefer a focused deep-dive into kernel/ops or a more balanced panel (design + coding + behavior)?

Thanks,
Sarah
TalentBridge Recruiting
(sarah@talentbridge.io)

Attachments: resume_liam_porter.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Fwd: Intro: Liam Porter — Senior Serving Engineer candidate  (panel & leveling input needed)

Forwarding Sarah's note and Liam's resume. Highlights below — please weigh in on scope and what we should use as pass/fail anchors for "Senior" vs "Staff". I want to finalize the interview rubric and schedule by EOD.

Why I think he's worth a panel:
- 6 years infra + 3 years focused on inference serving; shipped quantized kernels that reduced memory by 40% at RivenAI
- Strong ops background (on-call, perf regressions, incident runbooks)

Proposed panel outline (total 3.25h):
- Intro & behavioral (30m) — ownership, incident stories, cross-team tradeoffs
- System design (60m) — end-to-end serving architecture for a multi-tenant model deployment with cold-start constraints
- Inference deep-dive (45m) — kernel/quantization questions, memory/kv cache tradeoffs, practical quantization gotchas
- Live pairing / code exercise (40m) — small kernel optimization or simulating KV cache behavior

Specific asks for the group:
1) What are the non-negotiable signals for Senior here? (e.g., shipping to production alone, handling latency SLOs, clear ownership across infra + platform)
2) What distinguishes strong Senior from early Staff for us? (scope, ambiguous problem solving, impact level)
3) Any redlines (lack of ops experience, poor debugging methodology, shallow understanding of quantization)?

Attachments: candidate_scorecard_template.pdf, kernels_pair_prompt.md

--
Connor O'Brien
Hiring Manager — Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro: Liam Porter — Senior Serving Engineer candidate  (panel & leveling input needed)

Thanks for the forward — quick thoughts:

- Rubric edits: add explicit anchors per section (Design: tradeoff articulation + ops plan; Deep-dive: kernel correctness + measurable perf estimates; Pairing: clarity under time pressure). I'll update the scorecard template with 1-4 scale anchors.
- Pairing exercise: prefer a short, focused task (25-35m) that lets us observe reasoning and micro-optimizations (not a full build). The kernels_pair_prompt.md is a good start but trim it.
- Bar-raising: I can take the bar-raiser slot if we need independent calibration, but want a 10-min sync before the post-interview debrief so we align on the non-negotiables.

Redlines I care about: inability to reason about production failure modes, no evidence of ownership for latency regressions, or simplistic cost/throughput tradeoffs.

I'll prepare annotated anchors in the scorecard by EOD.

Marissa
Sr. Staff Engineer, Serving
Redwood Inference

From: Grace O'Connor <grace_oconnor@redwood.com>
To: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: Sat, 3 Apr 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Intro: Liam Porter — Senior Serving Engineer candidate  (panel & leveling input needed)

Echo Marissa. A few concrete calibration points I'd like the panel to watch for (these will be the anchors I use in the debrief):

Non-negotiable anchors (Senior):
- Demonstrated ownership: led a rollout or incident to resolution, wrote runbooks or mitigations
- Operational debugging: can triage p99 latency regressions with a clear hypothesis-driven approach
- Practical quantization knowledge: can explain accuracy/latency tradeoffs and pitfalls for int8/4-bit flows

Signals for early Staff (above Senior):
- Broad impact: influenced multiple product teams' serving strategy or owned cross-customer SLOs
- Architectural foresight: proposed and executed changes that materially changed cost or reliability at scale

On interview logistics: I'll handle the bar-raiser slot. Dev, can you take the live-pairing and own the environment (VM + dataset)? Connor — if we confirm times I'll send the calendar invites.

Grace
VP, Serving & Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Connor O'Brien <connor_obrien@redwood.com>
